headline_finding.statement: The Alt+G hotkey is a browser-global setting; Gemini entitlement is a per-profile setting. A browser-global control cannot make a per-profile guarantee.
headline_finding.source: chrome/browser/glic/glic_pref_names.cc: glic.launcher_enabled and glic.launcher_hotkey are registered in RegisterLocalStatePrefs (User Data\Local State, one per installation); glic.completed_fre is registered in RegisterProfilePrefs (User Data\Profile 2\Preferences, one per profile).
headline_finding.resolution: Do not steer the hotkey. Remove the ambiguity: gate on glic.completed_fre being completed on EXACTLY ONE profile, and that profile being the resolved Profile 2. Then the browser-global hotkey has only one profile it can open. See gate 7.
headline_finding.converts: an unguaranteeable requirement into a checkable precondition, the same move as cosmos_surfaces.qualify_backup_target

secondary_findings.statement: Alt+G is the published Windows accelerator for open/close Gemini in Chrome. cDeck must SEND it and must NEVER RegisterHotKey it.
secondary_findings.hazard: RegisterHotKey is exclusive. cDeck either loses with ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED (1409, silent if unchecked) or WINS and steals Alt+G from Chrome, breaking Keith's working native shortcut and forcing cDeck to synthesize the keystroke it just intercepted.

secondary_findings.statement: The shortcut is user-remappable and its current value lives in Local State under glic.launcher_hotkey as an accelerator string. Hardcoding Alt+G fails silently the day it is remapped.
secondary_findings.rule: Read glic.launcher_hotkey and send what it says; refuse HOTKEY_MISMATCH if it disagrees with what GEM is about to synthesize, printing both values.

secondary_findings.statement: Command::kOpenGlic was renamed Command::kPanelToggle with prevent_close = false. Pressing while open CLOSES the panel. cDeck has no channel to read panel state.
secondary_findings.consequence: Open-only semantics cannot be built honestly on an unobservable toggle. Label GEM a toggle. Do not send twice to 'make sure' - that reliably guarantees it is closed. State observability is not recoverable by ANY available surface, including Option B.

secondary_findings.statement: RegisterLocalStatePrefs registers kGlicLauncherEnabled as false; it is auto-enabled on onboarding acceptance only when Chrome is default browser or on the stable channel.
secondary_findings.consequence: 'the toolbar button works' and 'Alt+G works' are DIFFERENT FACTS. Gate 8 is the single most likely reason a correct implementation appears to do nothing.

A_native_accelerator.reason: the only surface that both exists and reaches the real signed-in profile

B_ui_automation_invoke.mechanism: UIA Invoke on the Gemini toolbar button of a known Profile 2 window; IDC_OPEN_GLIC is a per-window browser command and a window belongs to exactly one profile
B_ui_automation_invoke.buys: profile determinism with no uniqueness precondition and no dependence on kGlicHotkeyLocalScope
B_ui_automation_invoke.costs: COM via ctypes against UIAutomationCore - real weight against the stdlib-only house rule that cosmos_browser.py:17-19 already invokes to reject a websocket CDP client; also UI-fragile, binds to an accessible name Google renames
B_ui_automation_invoke.escalate_when: Keith genuinely needs two glic-entitled profiles, so gate 7 cannot be satisfied

C_cdp_openGlic.why_dead: From Chrome 136 --remote-debugging-port and --remote-debugging-pipe are IGNORED against the default Chrome data directory and must be paired with a non-standard --user-data-dir. A non-standard user-data-dir is a fresh profile that is not signed in. Gemini in Chrome is not available for Chrome profiles that are not signed-in. Therefore: automation surface XOR Gemini entitlement, never both.
C_cdp_openGlic.chain: CDP surface => non-default user-data-dir => profile not signed in => glic unavailable; Profile 2 => default user-data-dir => no CDP surface
C_cdp_openGlic.not_a_bug_to_wait_out: it is the intended effect of a deliberate anti-cookie-theft change; Google's stated alternative is Chrome for Testing, which is precisely not Keith's profile
corollaries: Do NOT attach a debugging port to Keith's real profile. The port has no authentication; anything that can reach it reads every cookie and live session in that profile.
This also kills the CDP-preflight hybrid. The section 5 preflight is therefore all file and registry reads, no browser attach.
GEM must NOT be built as a DomWorker job: DomWorker.run_attempt creates a fresh profile per attempt by contract (cosmos_dom.py:52-60), which is the exact thing that makes glic unavailable.

D_extension_side_panel.reason: chrome.sidePanel hosts an extension page; it cannot host Google's glic, no extension API invokes IDC_OPEN_GLIC, and embedding gemini.google.com inside it is blocked by X-Frame-Options

gates_not_locally_readable.region_and_language: US / en-US gradual rollout is a real eligibility gate but is not locally readable, so it is not a gate row. It surfaces as a dispatch that lands and produces no panel - which is exactly why the success return is TOGGLE_NOT_OBSERVABLE and not OK.

hotkey_scope.disabled_behavior: global hotkey handled by GlicBackgroundModeManager - handled AHEAD of the focused window, so focusing a Profile 2 window first does NOT make the dispatch profile-deterministic
hotkey_scope.enabled_behavior: scoped to Chrome-focused, handled by InstanceIndependentHotkeyManager - focus then determines the browser, so focus-first WOULD be profile-deterministic
hotkey_scope.consequence: cDeck does not control this flag, so it must not depend on either behavior. Gate 7 makes the dispatch correct under both.

typed_refusals.precedent_chosen: SurfaceError (cosmos_surfaces.py:44-54) defines its own kinds for its own domain; DomError (cosmos_dom.py:26-31) has a fixed four-word vocabulary. GEM is a new domain, so it follows SurfaceError with a GlicError(kind, detail), reusing UNREACHABLE and BROKE VERBATIM so the ledger vocabulary does not fork for concepts that already have words.

kinds.NOT_ADDRESSABLE: caller has no channel to browser UI (browser-served deck)
kinds.UNREACHABLE: no Chrome binary - reused from DomError
kinds.BROKE: mid-dispatch failure, outcome unestablished - reused from DomError, report-never-retry

success_return.why: GEM dispatched an accelerator; it cannot prove a panel opened. The tree is explicit that a screenshot is never proof of a paid action (cosmos_dom.py:9) and that evidence is EVIDENCE, not proof of a remote commitment (cosmos_dom.py:85-87). A keystroke is weaker evidence than a screenshot. Returning OK would be the green-log-over-nothing defect cosmos_surfaces was written to stop.

typed_refusals.verdict_spec_conformance: every refusal detail must be self-contained and name the exact file/symbol and the fix, per docs/VERDICT_SPEC.md:24 - Ara reads it aloud and Keith fixes it from the headphones with no desktop. 'doesn't work' is an invalid refusal.

browser_served_deck.why: a page served from Core :8770 runs in the renderer sandbox: it cannot synthesize OS keystrokes, read Local State, read the registry, enumerate windows, or invoke IDC_OPEN_GLIC. Nothing in the browser-served path can open a Chrome side panel. That is not a gap to close; it is the sandbox working.
browser_served_deck.shared_refusal: Core should own the refusal so both deck modes render the same object: a read-only GET /api/v1/gem/preflight returning the gate results as JSON. Read-only, additive, NOT APPLIED in this PR; Core :8770 stays up untouched.

clipboard.secure_context_holds: the tree serves the deck over HTTPS - phone_url is https://{FQDN}:8770/ (tests/test_up.py:95,137), and secure context is scheme-based so a self-signed cert still qualifies
caveats: the write must happen INSIDE the click handler, not after an await on the preflight fetch, or the activation is gone
if the deck is ever served over plain http:// to a LAN IP the API is absent entirely - keep a document.execCommand('copy') fallback on a hidden textarea
do not report 'copied' without checking the promise resolved
